get.description:
What a delete of ``slug`` would take, for the delete dialog: kind, title,

One document, through access.can(read).

Scope: a tenant token's workspace wins over ``X-Markdrop-Workspace`` (set by
the edge on a workspace's own domain; unsigned, so it can only narrow).

Renamed documents (Q4): a slug that is in some document's ``old_slugs``
answers — only to a caller who can read that document — ``200
{"moved": true, "slug": <current>, "url", "workspace_url", "folder_path"}``
with header ``X-Markdrop-Moved: <current>``; the page then 307s to the
canonical address. Anyone else gets exactly the denial the current slug
would give them (404 / 401 + gate), never the new slug.

delete.description:
A page with sub-pages needs ``?children=delete`` (they go too) or
``?children=lift`` (they move up a level); without it, 409
``{code: "has_children", count}``.

post.description:
A9: the owner replaces a leaked edit secret. The old one stops working
at once; the new one is returned once.
Attach an anonymous document to the logged-in account (proven via secret).

Import a copy of a readable document into the caller's account.

Owned by the caller with a fresh slug, no password and no expiry; born
private unless the source is plainly public (Q3). 404/401/403 exactly as a
read of the source would answer.

get.description:
Could the document at ``slug`` move to ``new_slug``? For whoever may
rename it (``PATCH …/slug``'s rule): ``{slug, current, available, code
(null | same | invalid | reserved | taken | folder), detail, url,
markdrop_url, workspace_url, redirects_from}`` — the links it would have
(its workspace's domain with folders and parent pages, when it is filed)
and the old slugs that already redirect to it.

patch.description:
A document's password and expiry, without its content (the share
dialog's "More options"). can(edit_settings): the owner or the edit
secret. Same transition as ``PUT /{slug}`` with those fields: a new
password narrows (epoch bump, bytes closed first, cache purge awaited);
removing it widens; an expiry books its purge. A past date is 422.

put.description:
Open a document in the block editor (``blocks``) or the classic one.
The Markdown is unchanged. can(edit_content); refused for encrypted
documents and files.

get.description:
The page's sub-pages this caller can read: ``[{slug, title, editor,
updated_at, has_children, access_inherit}]``, oldest first.

Pages that mention, embed or link to this one — only those this caller
can read: ``[{slug, title, editor, updated_at, kinds}]``.

Who the page's editor can @-mention (``@`` and ``/person`` in the page
editor): ``{state, people: [{id, name, email, avatar_url, you}]}``, the
members of the page's workspace, sorted by name. can(edit_content).

``state`` is ``ok``; ``signin`` for an edit-link editor with no account;
``personal`` for a page in no workspace; ``not_member`` for someone who
edits it (a grant, the edit link) but isn't a member of its workspace.
Only ``ok`` lists anyone. ``email`` is filled in for a signed-in member on
markdrop.in only, never on the workspace's own domain (as ``/auth/me``).

put.description:
Put the page under another page (``parent``: its slug) or at the top
(null). 409 ``{code: "access_change", readers_before, readers_after}`` when
that changes who can read it, unless ``confirm_access_change``.

post.description:
An image for the page (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 10 MB):
``{id, mime, size, width, height}``; write it as ``![alt](asset:<id>)``.
can(edit_content).

get.description:
Fresh links for the page images its content references (signed ones
expire with an artifact link's lifetime): ``{assets: {id: {url, expires_at}}}``.

post.description:
What this viewer may see of each embedded item (``{embeds: {slug:
Resolved}}``). The caller must be able to read the page; each item is then
resolved with the item's own access, for this caller. Anything not "ok"
carries no title, excerpt or link.

Take, renew or take over the page's edit lock (services/pages.acquire_lock).

The block editor takes it with its first real change (``intent=edit``) and renews it every
30 s (``intent=heartbeat`` with ``edited``: it changed something since, ``hidden``: its tab is
hidden, ``dirty``: it has unsaved changes). It holds until 2 minutes after the last heartbeat,
2 minutes after the last change or 60 seconds after the tab was hidden, whichever is first.
Answers ``{holder: {name}, expires_at, mine: true, rev, timers}``; a heartbeat for a lock that
lapsed or was taken over answers ``{mine: false, released: true, reason}`` (it never takes it
back). 423 ``{code: "locked", holder, idle_s, dirty, releases_in_s, can_take_over, …}`` while
someone else holds it. ``take_over=true``: the page's owner or a workspace admin takes it (403
``take_over_forbidden`` for anyone else); the other editor is told and keeps its unsaved text.

get.description:
Who holds the page's edit lock, without taking it (can(edit_content)): ``{holder: null}``
when it's free, else the holder, ``idle_s``, ``dirty``, ``releases_in_s``, ``mine`` and
``can_take_over``; ``taken_over`` when the caller's own lock was taken in the last hour.

post.description:
Keep an editor's unsaved text that it can't save (its lock was taken over, or someone else
holds the page now) as a version in the page's history, labelled as such. The page itself is
unchanged. ``{version, kept}`` (``kept: false`` when the text is already the page or its newest
version).

``DELETE …/lock`` for a page that is closing. The browser sends it with
``navigator.sendBeacon``: a keepalive DELETE needs a CORS preflight that
browsers don't make while a page unloads, and a beacon can't carry an
Authorization header, so the text/plain body says who is leaving:

* the ``release_token`` the lock's answers carry (services/tickets.py): it
  lets go of that person's own lock on this one page and nothing else, on
  markdrop.in and on a workspace's own domain alike (the editor sends this);
* or, from editors loaded before release tokens, the session token itself: the
  markdrop.in session, or a workspace domain's tenant token sent from that
  domain (its Origin must be the token's host, the host must still be live,
  and the page must be in the token's workspace — the same three checks as
  any tenant request).

Anything else (no token, an API token, a token for another page, someone
else's lock) is ignored; the answer is always 204.

Flag a document for abuse (public, rate-limited). Always 202; stored
only when the slug exists.

A new page (``editor: "blocks"``). ``template`` fills it from a built-in
template (``{{date}}`` / ``{{title}}`` filled in); ``content`` gives its
Markdown instead. ``workspace`` (member+) and ``folder`` file it there;
``parent`` (the slug of a page you can edit) puts it inside that page, in
its workspace and folder, inheriting its access. ``slug`` gives it its link
(publish's custom-slug rules; 409 when taken, nothing is created). Unless it
has a cover (or ``auto_cover`` is false, or its workspace turned Auto covers
off), a cover is picked for it in the background: ``cover_pending``.

get.description:
The page's cover now, for an editor waiting on an auto cover: ``{cover, cover_auto,
cover_pending, rev}`` (anyone who can read it).

post.description:
A cover for the page, picked like an auto cover, not written (the cover picker's "Pick for
me"): ``{cover: "gallery:<id>", how}``. Editors only.

get.description: The built-in templates: ``[{id, name, description, icon, category, content}]``.

post.description:
Save a copy of the page (and, with ``include_subpages``, the sub-pages
you can open) as a template: the workspace's (members and up) or your own.
Its images are copied with it.

get.description:
The New page gallery: ``{builtin, workspace, personal, workspace_id,
workspace_name, workspace_role, can_save_workspace, can_reorder_workspace,
folder}``. ``workspace`` lists that workspace's templates when you're a
member (not a viewer) of it; ``folder`` (an id or path of it) adds
``folder: {id, name, default_template, can_set_default}``. ``parent`` (a
page's slug: Add a sub-page) reads both from that page instead, which you
must be able to read. On a workspace's own domain ``parent`` is required,
and the gallery offers the built-ins and that workspace's templates.

One workspace or personal template with its Markdown and image links (the preview). On a
workspace's own domain: that workspace's templates only.

patch.description:
Rename it, or change its description or icon (an empty icon clears it).
Workspace templates: its admins and whoever saved it.

delete.description: Delete a template and its sub-pages. Pages made from it stay as they are.

put.description: Reorder a workspace's templates (admins) or your personal ones.

Turn this page itself into a template (``true``: it leaves every list
and search and shows in the New page gallery; its sub-pages come with it)
or back into a page (``false``). Pages made from it never change.

What New page in this folder starts from (admins). The person making a
page can still choose blank or another template.

get.description:
What the UI may offer: ``{enabled, reason, message, can_write, can_ask, vision, actions, tones,
languages}``. ``reason``: signin | encrypted | off | not_configured | workspace_off | blocked |
daily | monthly.

``{versions: [{n, ts, author: {kind, id, name, client, label, picture},
title, icon, bytes, restored_from, current}], next_cursor, available,
reason}``, newest first; pass ``next_cursor`` back as ``cursor`` for older

One version: its Markdown and image links, plus ``current_doc`` (the

post.description:
Make version ``n`` the page again, as a new version (the page as it was
is kept first, so this can be undone). 423 ``{code: "locked", holder}``
while someone else has the page open in the editor.

get.description:
The page's sign-off blocks for this viewer: ``{signoffs: [{block, label,
options, lock, person, option, tone, signed_at, signed_by, can_sign,
can_remove, history}]}``. Names (person, signer, history) only for people
inside the page's circle, like ``:person`` mentions. The decision comes from
the server, never from the Markdown.

post.description:
The person the block names chooses an option (``{option: null}``
clears it). 403 for anyone else, 404 for a block that isn't on the page, 422
for an option the block doesn't offer. Returns the block as they see it.

get.description: The page as a file to download (see the module docstring).

An export link from ``export_page`` (MCP), for the user it was made for. A browser that
opens a link which no longer works gets a short page saying so (an API client, the JSON).

post.description:
``{url, title, description, site_name, favicon, image, fetched}`` for a
bookmark block. Signed in only. 422 for an address that may not be fetched
(private networks, other schemes or ports, credentials in the URL).

get.description: The providers a page may embed: ``[{id, name, example}]``.

``{provider, name, embed_url, aspect_ratio, url}`` for an allowlisted
link (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma, Google Maps embed links, CodePen); 422
for anything else. Computed from the link alone: nothing is fetched.

post.description: The same as ``POST /api/v1/bookmarks/preview`` (one limit budget each).

get.description: Feature gate + quota for the UI. Safe to call when nothing is configured.

post.description: Verify the uploaded blob, then publish it at a slug.

Publish pasted HTML directly — the most-requested flow.

Small enough that a presigned round trip would be pointless; anything larger
should go through the file-upload path.

patch.description:
Edit an artifact's title (owner, editors, members on non-private files)
or its password / expiry (owner only, A3).

Separate from the markdown update route because that one requires a
`content` body, which an artifact doesn't have. Publicity, the access epoch,
cache purges and live events follow from services/transitions.py.

put.description:
Add or replace a video's captions (a .vtt or .srt file's text): the player shows them as
subtitles, and search and Ask read them by minute. can(edit_content) on the file.

Swap the file behind an artifact, keeping its URL and settings.

Single file → single file: can(replace_file) — the owner, editor grantees
and workspace members on non-private files (Q6); counted against the
**owner's** quota, and a non-owner whose upload would need the owner's old
versions dropped gets 507 instead. Either side a zipped site:
can(replace_bundle) — owner only.

Same verify-then-commit shape as creation: the object is HEADed for its real
size and type before anything is written, and the previous object (or bundle
prefix) is freed only once the swap has succeeded.

post.description:
200 with the result, or 202 ``{state: "verifying", upload_id}`` when the
sha256 check outlasts the wait: poll ``GET /uploads/{id}`` until ``state``
is "done" (``result``) or "failed" (``error``). Calling it again on a
finished upload returns the same result.

delete.description:
Delete an old version to free its space. Owner only: editors may restore
a version but not destroy one, and the space is the owner's. Never the
current version (409).

get.description:
Render an ASCII/box-drawing diagram to PNG.

Public and unauthenticated by design: Google's markdown→Doc converter fetches
this URL anonymously while importing an exported document. The diagram text is
carried (compressed) in ``d`` — nothing is read from the database.

Render a Mermaid diagram to PNG (public — Google's converter fetches it).

Delegates to Kroki server-side; on any failure we fall back to rendering the
Mermaid source as a monospace image so the export never silently loses it.
Render a LaTeX expression to PNG (public — Google's converter fetches it).

Return the Google consent URL. The frontend redirects the browser to it.

The logged-in user id is signed into the OAuth ``state`` so the callback can
attribute the returned refresh token without an Authorization header.
Handle Google's redirect: store the encrypted refresh token on the user.

post.description:
Revoke the grant at Google, then forget the stored token.

We revoke on Google's side first so the user is fully disconnected (the app
loses all Drive access), then clear locally regardless of whether the revoke
call succeeded — a dead/network-failed token must not leave the account stuck
in a "connected" state.

Create the linked Google Doc, or refresh it from the current content.

First call creates a Doc (Phase 1). Subsequent calls update the same Doc
in place (Phase 2). Markdown stays the source of truth.

patch.description: Set the display name (used for passwordless email accounts with no name).

get.description: Redirect the browser to Google's consent screen.
Handle Google's redirect: exchange code, upsert user, issue our session.

post.description: Email the caller a login code + magic link. Always returns {status: sent}.
Verify a 6-digit OTP and return a session token (used by the frontend form).

get.description: Consume a magic link and redirect to the frontend with a session token.

One-click opt-out of bulk email. Public by design.

Mail clients hit this unauthenticated via List-Unsubscribe, so authority
comes from the signed token (HMAC(AUTH_SECRET, "unsub:{uid}")) rather than a
session. It only ever stops mail, so there is nothing to escalate even if a
link leaks. Transactional mail (sign-in codes, invitations) is unaffected:
those are never bulk sends.

Also served at /api/v1/unsubscribe (``unsubscribe_alias_router`` below):
campaigns sent before the URL fix link there.

post.description: RFC 8058 one-click: some clients POST rather than GET.

get.description:
Aggregated analytics: can(view_stats) — the owner only. A reader who
isn't the owner gets 403, anyone else the read denial (404).

Up to 50 people to suggest in the share dialog.

Only two sources, both people the caller already has a relationship with:
addresses they have granted document access to themselves, and members of
workspaces they belong to (whom any member can already list). It is never a
search over all users -- that would turn the share box into an oracle for
"does this address have an account here". For the same reason a grant-only
contact carries no name: the share list never showed one either.

`q` narrows by case-insensitive substring of email or name. Most recently
shared-with first, then co-members by name. The caller is never included.

post.description: Create a personal API token (raw value returned once).

get.description:
A frame of the owner's video at ``t`` seconds (rounded), as a JPEG.
404 when it isn't a video, or frames can't be made here.

comes, per kind (``email_notify``: ``{mention, signoff_requested}`` → instant | hourly | daily |
off; services/notifications.py); the old switch ``mention_emails`` (bool: off turns both off,
on brings back the defaults); ``tz`` (the browser's timezone, for the daily digest). Any of them.

The "Turn off weekly emails" link. It asks before acting: mail scanners
open every link in an email, and a GET that acted would turn the email off
for people who never clicked. The button (and one-click) POSTs.

post.description: The page's button, and RFC 8058 one-click from List-Unsubscribe-Post.

get.description: Can Analytics AI run for the caller now, and where they may see content gaps.
What changed in the range and why, in 3-5 bullets (cached for the day; ``fresh=1`` refreshes).

post.description: Ask your analytics (SSE). The model picks from a fixed set of queries; ours run them.

get.description: What people searched for or asked and didn't find, grouped into pages worth writing.
The cached analysis of this kind, or whether one can be made (never calls the model).

Analyse (Claude Haiku 5.5) unless a cached analysis exists; ``{"refresh": true}`` in the
body re-analyses. Below 20 sessions with data the model isn't called (``state: thin``).

get.description:
The bell polls this only while a tab is visible: the person has seen what came before
(no email about it), and ``tz`` (their IANA zone) times the daily digest.

Asks first: mail scanners open every link, and a GET that acted would
turn the emails off for people who never clicked.
Asks first, like the turn-off link: a mail scanner opening it changes nothing.

(``endpoint``: this browser's own, marked ``this_device``) and which kinds they want.

post.description:
The service worker calls this when someone clicks a notification: the signed link (made
for that person and those notifications only) marks them read. No session: the worker has none.

Create + link a document from the editor (owned by the caller).

A markdown file becomes a markdown document; an .html (or other text
artifact) file becomes an artifact, so it publishes as a rendered page
rather than as escaped source. Both sync through the same endpoints below,
so the editor needs no second protocol.

get.description: Full pull of the current server content.

get.description: Cheap revision check for polling.

post.description: Record a bug report or feature request. Always returns {status: received}.

delete.description:
Delete a workspace and everything that belongs to it.

Shared documents are released, not deleted -- they belong to their owners,
not to the workspace.

get.description:
People to @-mention in a page (``:person[Name]{id="…"}``): members whose
name or address matches ``q``, as ``[{id, name, avatar}]`` (never the
address). Members of the workspace only; at most 20.

post.description:
Invite someone by email.

Rate-limited by the hour rather than the minute, because the thing being
spent here is not our CPU — it is someone else's inbox, and this endpoint
will happily send mail to an address its caller does not own.

Upload a favicon or logo.

The stored URL is returned but not saved onto the workspace here: the
settings form owns that, and saving a field the user hasn't confirmed would
make "upload, change your mind, close the tab" leave the wrong logo live.

Attach a verified host so the edge will terminate TLS for it.

Returns 501 rather than a 500 when no hosting credentials are configured:
that is a deployment that hasn't enabled the integration, not a fault, and
the caller should be told to finish the step by hand.
Take a verified domain off the air without discarding its verification.

get.description:
Which DNS panel this customer is about to open.

A separate endpoint rather than a field on the domain list, because it costs
a live DNS lookup and the list is rendered on every visit to the tab. The UI
asks for it only while the setup instructions are actually on screen, and
only admins see those.

put.description:
Choose the domain this workspace is addressed by.

Admin, because it changes the address printed on every preview card and
handed out by the library — the workspace's public face, not one person's
preference.

delete.description:
``trash`` (the default): the folder, its folders and everything in them
go to the trash for 30 days (services/trash.py), restorable together.
``unfile`` / ``move_up`` (the old behaviour): only the folder goes; what was
in it moves to the top of the workspace / into the parent folder.

patch.description:

(A10). The subtree's depth is validated, every document below gets its new
path, and all of them are purged.

get.description:
The app rail's outline: every readable top-level item, compact, grouped by folder
(``{items: [{slug, title, kind: page|markdown|artifact, folder_id, has_children, icon,
icon_url, renderer, mime, filename}], more: {<folder id>|root: n}}``). Viewer+.

post.description:
What the Cards view shows of each item: ``{previews: {slug: preview}}``
(services/card_preview.py). The app asks only for the cards on screen.
Viewer+, like the listing; each item answers ``locked`` unless the caller
can open it right now (no password, no sign-in, no refusal in the way),
``encrypted`` for end-to-end encrypted documents, ``pending`` while a
picture is being made, else ``ok`` with plain-text blocks, a sheet's first
cells, a text file's first lines, a small WebP thumbnail (``src``, a data

from them and why — among the items the caller can see (services/preview.py).
Member+; ``as=email`` admin+ (it reveals that person's grants).

post.description:
Batch refile (drag-and-drop): member+ for documents they can read. All
are checked before any moves; one refusal refuses the batch.

``access`` is given.

including redacted rows, by ``handles`` (``id_token`` from /items).

put.description:

get.description: The folder's share (same shape as the PUT), or 404 when not shared.

get.description:

breadcrumbs:[{name, path}]}, subfolders:[{name, path, count}], items:[{slug,
title, kind, mime, url, size_bytes?, updated_at, poster_url?}]}`` — paths
relative to the shared root; items filtered to what this caller can read.

people, links, can_edit_schema, role}``. Rows are the top-level pages filed

pages are never changed: a property left out keeps its values, hidden.
Replace the folder's saved views (members and admins; at most 20).

get.description: The page's properties panel for this reader (null: none).

``{results:[{slug, ok, error?}]}``.

and the grantee list are not something a link exposes. Viewers see their
own role and the owner's display name; the grantee list (and the owner's

only).

Claude Haiku's verdict on the section against these decisions: ``contradicts`` / ``omits`` /
``consistent`` with a one-line note. Never edits the page.

get.description:
Your switches: ``panel`` (the "From meetings" panel shows by itself) and ``hints`` (suggestions
when a section seems to leave out a decision). Both on by default.

post.description: Mark one of your action items or targets done: it leaves your open items, the board and "This week".

get.description:
The workspace's Team groups; for admins also ``suggestions``: a group per meeting series, of the
members at half or more of its meetings in the last 60 days.

post.description:
This week's summary now (it goes out on its own on Mondays at 9 am, workspace time): posted to the
Slack meetings channel when Slack is connected, emailed to the admins, kept as Team's "This week".

get.summary: The Slack workspace a link page is for

get.description:
Off by default. ``teams``: the Slack workspaces connected to Markdrop workspaces you belong to,
and whether Markdrop found you there.

put.summary: Turn my Slack notifications on or off
put.description:
On: Markdrop looks you up by your own sign-in email in each connected Slack workspace
(``results`` says what it found per team; nothing about any other address). Only you can turn
yours on.

post.description:
Who can edit the meeting's page may post it (again) to the workspace's meetings channel. The
channel rule still applies: a meeting the whole channel may not see is never posted.

get.description: What the home's Ask box needs: whether AI can answer now, suggested questions, recent ones.

post.description: Ask a question (a follow-up with ``thread_id``); the answer streams as Server-Sent Events.

get.description:
What the assistant offers where you are: its scopes (This doc, Meetings, This folder, Workspace,
Everything) for things you can open, the default one, the workspace's meeting series, whether you
can insert answers into the doc, and whether AI can answer now (AI search and Meetings AI).

Suggested questions for Ask. With ``workspace``: its team questions, refreshed from what happened
there in the last 7 days (meetings and pages every member can read; one list for all members), and
yours (your action items, your latest meeting). Without: yours, across your workspaces.
Your recent questions, newest first.
One conversation, its sources decided again for you now.

What the home shows, decided for you: unread notifications and access requests waiting on you
(``attention``), the open to-dos that mention you in pages you can read (``actions``; ``can_tick``
when you may edit the page), the latest meetings across your workspaces (``meetings``), your
workspaces with people, item and meeting counts (``workspaces``) and whether Google Meet is
connected (``meet``). No AI.

post.description:
Mark one of your to-dos done (``- [ ]`` → ``- [x]``, found by its block id) through the normal
save path; ``done: false`` opens it again. 404: the page or to-do is gone (or you can't open it);
403: you can't edit the page, or the to-do doesn't mention you; 409: already that way; 423: someone
is editing the page.

Card previews (as ``POST /workspaces/{id}/items/previews``) for items anywhere: your own, shared
with you, in any workspace. Each answers ``locked`` unless you can open it right now.

AccessSync.title: AccessSync
AccessSync.description:
A sign-in change (Team/Open ⇄ Locked) still being carried through to
stored files, page images and cached pages. The gate itself holds from the
moment the setting is saved; this is what the settings page shows as
"Applying to N items…".

ArtifactCreateRequest.title: ArtifactCreateRequest
ArtifactCreateRequest.description: Step 2: confirm an uploaded blob and mint the shareable document.

ArtifactPasteRequest.title: ArtifactPasteRequest
ArtifactPasteRequest.description: Paste-an-HTML-page shortcut — no presigned round trip for small pages.

ArtifactReplaceRequest.title: ArtifactReplaceRequest
ArtifactReplaceRequest.description: Swap the underlying file while keeping the slug, password and expiry.

ArtifactSettingsRequest.title: ArtifactSettingsRequest
ArtifactSettingsRequest.description:
Owner-editable settings. Every field is optional — omitted means unchanged.

Separate from ``DocumentUpdate`` because that schema requires ``content``,
which an artifact doesn't have (its bytes live in R2).

ArtifactStatusResponse.title: ArtifactStatusResponse
ArtifactStatusResponse.description: Drives UI gating — the feature stays hidden until R2 is wired up.

ArtifactUploadUrlRequest.title: ArtifactUploadUrlRequest
ArtifactUploadUrlRequest.description: Step 1 of the upload: ask for a presigned PUT.

BrandingPayload.title: BrandingPayload
BrandingPayload.description: Every field optional — an unset workspace looks exactly like Markdrop.

CaptionsRequest.title: CaptionsRequest
CaptionsRequest.description: A video's captions: the text of a .vtt or .srt file (services/captions.py).

ContactItem.title: ContactItem
ContactItem.description:
Someone the signed-in user may be offered as a share suggestion.

Only ever drawn from people the user already has a relationship with — see
`routers.me.list_contacts`. Never a global user search.

text.title: Text
text.description: The right version (optional): shown instead of the line.

DnsProviderHint.title: DnsProviderHint
DnsProviderHint.description:
Who runs this domain's DNS, so the instructions can use their words.

Everything is optional: an unrecognised provider falls back to the generic
instructions, which is what every customer sees today.

DocumentSettingsRequest.title: DocumentSettingsRequest
DocumentSettingsRequest.description:
``PATCH /documents/{slug}/settings``: a document's password and expiry
without resending its content (the share dialog's "More options"). Every
field is optional; omitted means unchanged. ``read_password: ""`` removes
the password, like ``remove_password: true``.

on_conflict.title: On Conflict
on_conflict.description: When the folder's address is already taken where it goes: `error` (default) returns 409 saying what holds it; `suffix` takes the next free address (name-2, name-3…).

on_conflict.title: On Conflict
on_conflict.description: When the folder's address is already taken where it goes: `error` (default) returns 409 saying what holds it; `suffix` takes the next free address (name-2, name-3…).

on_conflict.title: On Conflict
on_conflict.description: When the folder's address is already taken where it goes: `error` (default) returns 409 saying what holds it; `suffix` takes the next free address (name-2, name-3…).

InvitePreview.title: InvitePreview
InvitePreview.description:
What the person holding the link is shown before deciding.

Names the workspace, the inviter and the address it was sent to, and nothing
else — in particular not who else is a member. The recipient already knows
their own address; everything here was in the email they were sent.

InviteResponse.title: InviteResponse
InviteResponse.description:
The admin-facing view of an invitation. Deliberately has no token field:
the raw token exists for exactly as long as it takes to compose the email,
and putting it in an API response would turn any workspace admin into a
credential oracle for an address they do not control.

LockKeepRequest.title: LockKeepRequest
LockKeepRequest.description:
An editor's unsaved text it can't save (its lock was taken over, or someone else holds the
page now): kept as a version in the page's history (services/pages.keep_unsaved).

PreferencesUpdate.title: PreferencesUpdate
PreferencesUpdate.description:
Any of these; what's left out is unchanged. ``tz``: the browser's IANA timezone (the daily
digest goes at 08:00 there).

page.title: Page
page.description: The page being written (its slug): its workspace, and its own meeting left out.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: A workspace id, when there is no page.

heading.title: Heading
heading.description: The heading of the section under the caret.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: meetings / folder / workspace: the workspace id

folder.title: Folder

SignRequest.title: SignRequest
SignRequest.description: ``option``: one of the block's options; null clears the decision.

WorkspaceDeleteRequest.title: WorkspaceDeleteRequest
WorkspaceDeleteRequest.description: The workspace's own name, typed back. See `services.workspace.delete_workspace`.

page.title: Page
page.description: Ask AI in this page (its slug): the page, then its workspace's meetings (recorded decisions first) and documents. Implies intent "page".

scope.description: What to answer from (the assistant). Without it: everything (or `page`).

until.title: Until
until.description: When it stops applying (ISO time); none: until cleared.
